title: Relative integral closure over a separably closed valuation field
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $x\in K^\times$, either $x\in V$ or $x^{-1}\in V$. Let $A$ be a flat finitely presented commutative $V$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose $A_K=A\otimes_V K$ is geometrically reduced, meaning that $A_K\otimes_K E$ is reduced for every field extension $E/K$; reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent element. Regard $A$ as a subring of $A_K$. Put $B=\{b\in A_K: b\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in }A\}$. Then $B$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $B$ is a flat finitely presented $V$-algebra, the canonical map $B\otimes_V K\to A_K$ is an isomorphism, and $B\otimes_V\Omega$ is reduced for every homomorphism $V\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field. The valuation may have arbitrary height. The zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 2–4 (height-one analytic finiteness, decompletion, and finite-height composition) and the valuation-limit part of Step 5, printed pp. 22–24. Only the separably closed valuation-field case is asserted. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

from.place: Historical creation chain through lem-trf-valuation-curve-finite-normalization: Temkin §4.1 opening paragraph uses Theorem 3.5.5 to prove finiteness of normalization. This is a general scheme-theoretic tool of that normalization argument, not a realization of the current contracting-correspondence statement of lem-trf-local-term-locality. Supporting ingredient: Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 2–4 (height-one analytic finiteness, decompletion, and finite-height composition) and the valuation-limit part of Step 5, printed pp. 22–24. Only the separably closed valuation-field case is asserted.
